title: Sum an array with threads
description: Write `long long parallel_sum(const int *values, size_t count, int threads)` that splits the array into `threads` nearly equal parts, adds each part in its own C11 thread (`thrd_create`), joins them all and returns the total. Each thread writes only its own partial sum. `threads` is at least 1 and may be more than `count`.
hints: The part for thread `t` runs from `count * t / threads` to `count * (t + 1) / threads`: the parts cover everything with no gaps, even when `count` does not divide evenly.
Keep one small struct per thread (its range and its sum) in an array, pass `&parts[t]` to `thrd_create`, and add the sums up after `thrd_join`.
unitTests:
TEST("sums") { int v[10]; for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) v[i] = i + 1; CHECK_EQ((long)parallel_sum(v, 10, 3), 55L); CHECK_EQ((long)parallel_sum(v, 10, 1), 55L); CHECK_EQ((long)parallel_sum(v, 10, 16), 55L); CHECK_EQ((long)parallel_sum(v, 0, 4), 0L); }
TEST("a big array") { size_t n = 1000000; int *v = malloc(n * sizeof *v); for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) v[i] = (int)(i % 1000) - 500; long long expected = 0; for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) expected += v[i]; CHECK_EQ((long)parallel_sum(v, n, 4), (long)expected); free(v); }
